In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of mutants that have lost the ability to methylate the 2'-amino-adenine of 16S rRNA.
the elucidation of the mechanism by which kasugamycin exerts its effect.
the isolation, characterization and molecular analysis of kasugamycin resistant Bacillus stearothemophilus mutants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
kasugamycin resistance in B. st. and E. coli is connected with the absence of a dimethylation at two adjacent adenosine residues in 16S rRNA.
kasugamycin resistance in B. steraothermophilus and E. coli is due to the lack of dimethylation of 2 adjacent A’s in the 16s rRNA.
kasugamycin resistance in B. st. is due to the lack of dimethylation of A1408 and A1409 in the 16s r-RNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have isolated kasugamycin resistant B. stearothemophilus mutants, that we have identified one mutant lacking the enzyme for 2'-0,2'-0 dimethylation of adenosines 1518 and 1519, and that all kasugamycin resistance mutants analyzed biochemically lacked the enzyme that is responsible for the dimethylation.
kasugamycin is not a specific inhibitor of protein synthesis, but a specific inhibitor of the translation of the 16S rRNA.
kasugamycin is an antibiotic which inhibits protein synthesis in prokaryotes by binding to the ribosome and preventing initiation of protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kasugamycin resistance phenotype in Bacillus stearo-thermophilus is due to loss of dimethylation at A1518 and A1519 in 16S rRNA.

we have isolated kasugamycin resistant strains of Bacillus steraothermophilus that are deficient in the enzyme that catalyzes the dimethylation of 2 adjacent adenosines (A1518 and A1519) in the 16s rRNA.
the resistance to kasugamyin is due to the absence of the enzyme that is responsible for the methylation.
